title: Principality of Schwarzburg-Sonderhausen
capsule: The Principality of Schwarzburg-Sonderhausen was a small German state in Thuringia, one of two principalities of the House of Schwarzburg (the other being Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt), member of the German Confederation from 1815. Its princes ruled under a conservative constitutional framework through the revolutionary era of 1848–1849, emerging without territorial change. The principality joined the North German Confederation in 1866 after Prussia's defeat of Austria and entered the German Empire on 18 January 1871, retaining its hereditary prince but surrendering military and foreign policy sovereignty to Berlin. The reigning dynasty, from Gunther Friedrich Karl II through Günther (who died without a male heir in 1925), maintained the title until the Weimar-era abolition of German princely privileges in 1918.
